parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national layer (passport/visa sex-marker rules, entry refusal on 'reasonable doubt' about sex with a possible lifetime fraud finding, documented trans detainees abused in immigration custody, conversion-style federal inmate policies, official 'gender ideology' threat-framing) with a division layer adding a 2024 facility ban expanded to universities in 2026, birth-sex prison treatment restrictions, and no state hate-crime statute. Worst features are tier-1/tier-2: state-imposed facility exclusion by birth sex (trespass possible, one documented arrest) and border document friction — universal exposures for outed visitors. Mitigating: functioning courts granting trans plaintiffs relief (bathroom injunction, stay denied), national hate-crime and employment protections, no documented trans-specific violence pattern, and private venues largely uncovered.

entry_documents.exposure: Visa/entry cable directs refusal where documents or records raise 'reasonable doubt' about sex, plus possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; national passport marker policy restricted to M/F at birth; trans travellers report blocked/confiscated passports. Foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waiver and is never automatic; litigation ongoing in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate into fraud investigation → detention → birth-sex placement or conversion-style custody treatment.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans people in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-style treatment policies (hair, hormones, psychiatric drugs) from 2026; trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented detention of visitors for presentation alone in this division; trespass requires refusal to depart after notice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or ID mismatch can move a visitor into the federal custody system where these documented practices operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division facility ban (2024) expanded to public schools, colleges and universities (signed 15 May 2026); nationally, 9+1 units ban gender-congruent facility use in all government buildings and 4 units criminalise it; trespass carries up to 60 days, with one documented 2025 arrest (24h held in men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division ban reaches students in public institutions and government settings, not general private venues; trespass needs willful entry plus refusal to leave; national appellate injunction protects one student plaintiff and the state's stay request was denied.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering a capitol, courthouse or public campus restroom risks arrest; enforcement against non-students is uneven and unsettled.

care_services.exposure: Executive order frames gender-affirming care for minors as 'mutilation'; October 2025 proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for trans under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 hospital records; specialized LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut down.
care_services.protection: Proposed rules unresolved and several orders enjoined; no documented refusal of emergency care to trans visitors in this division.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor seeking care can become an investigated subject; care records exposure interacts with border/ID scrutiny.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ memo uses 'radical gender ideology' language; 66% public support for birth-sex document laws; division lacks a hate-crime statute; domestic-violence statutes cover only opposite-sex couples.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling and 22+units' nondiscrimination laws; the reward criterion is offences, not ideology; courts have blocked or enjoined several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that a routine stop or service denial becomes hostile, while federal hate-crime law supplies a partial remedy.

minors_guardians.exposure: EO directs law enforcement to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; division requires birth-sex restrooms in public schools; care for trans minors restricted; hospital records of under-19s subpoenaed.
minors_guardians.protection: Prosecutorial EO is aimed at in-school facilitation, not travelling families; no documented enforcement against visiting trans minors or parents.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor enrolled even briefly in a public campus setting, or any care encounter, can trigger the school/care enforcement chain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data for the division; official rhetoric and unrepealed sodomy provision supply social license; 23 units cover gender identity in bias-motivated-violence statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute operational; national travel guide advises checking reports but records no sodomy-law enforcement; division's own record shows no documented trans killings.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state hate-crime coverage weakens response quality if an assault occurs, though federal charging remains available.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division's hate-crime absence confirmed only by a 2007 source; no cell-placement case law recorded; freeze-frame treatment policies unremedied; litigation volatility means the operative rule set may change by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts demonstrably work for trans litigants (injunction upheld, stay denied); legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules; several national orders blocked or enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts mitigate the facility and school rules but not the border cable, which operates administratively at posts abroad.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra's register bars entry categorically with near-zero remedy. Here entry refusal is discretionary, tied to document discrepancy, requires a four-element fraud finding with waiver, and is actively litigated. No analogue to the universal, no-appeal exclusion register exists.

Similar in structure — secondary screening, discretionary refusal, slow remedies, officer discretion — but more severe: the dossier adds a lifetime-ineligibility threat, documented trans abuse in immigration custody, and state-level criminal facility exposure, while Kestrel Isles stops at administrative return.

Below 0.75-C: Meridia's border officers are trained, detention brief, with counsel and compensation. Here officers are affirmatively instructed to doubt sex, custody records show abuse of trans detainees, and the division criminalises facility use — features 0.75-C lacks entirely.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-level system: a national layer that engineers discovery probability (sex-doubt visa refusals, M/F-only markers, hostile official framing, trans-specific abuse documented in immigration custody) and a division layer adding birth-sex facility rules reaching public campuses and government buildings, with a trespass misdemeanour and one real arrest behind them. Severity is capped: no imprisonment likely for mere presentation, functioning courts grant trans plaintiffs relief, national hate-crime and employment protections remain, and private daily life is largely uncovered. Universal border and facility exposures without a documented working remedy keep this in Elevated Risk, not Reduced Risk; active litigation and uneven enforcement prevent it falling further.
